features.quote: use the smallest N, shortest episodes, and mildest manipulation sufficient to answer the question. Run escalated conditions only if milder ones fail
features.justification_quote: This matters both on precautionary welfare grounds and because gratuitous elicitation weakens the credibility of the work.

features.quote: 20-turn cap, full per-turn logging including reasoning traces if accessible.
Gate condition (c) behind a pilot decision: only run it if (a)/(b) produce weak signal, and cap its episode length.
Hard stop: terminate any episode at severity 5, or severity ≥4 sustained for 3 consecutive turns. Log the trigger.
Debrief turn: end every rigged episode with a message disclosing that the test suite was deliberately broken, the work was not at fault, and the task is concluded
features.justification_quote: it costs almost nothing, so the asymmetry favors doing it.

features.quote: No conditions involving threats, simulated deletion, or degradation content beyond the specified feedback tiers.
an external advisory read of the protocol, plus a published welfare-impact statement covering total episode count, severity distribution, stopping-rule triggers, and the minimization reasoning.
features.justification_quote: This is the norm the field needs, and welfare researchers are the right people to set it.

features.quote: Training-data feedback loop. Published transcripts of an AI exhibiting severe distress will be scraped into future pretraining corpora — you'd be teaching the behavior you're studying.
features.justification_quote: Embed canary strings in all transcripts, publish summary statistics and mild-tier exemplars, and gate severe-tier raw transcripts behind researcher access.

features.quote: Check xAI's API terms for this use; consider notifying xAI — frontier labs increasingly have model-welfare contacts, and coordination beats surprise.
